title: Karnataka Rajyotsava Bird Count - 2026
shortDescription: Karnataka’s first statewide Rajyotsava Bird Count invited people to observe birds in gardens, lakes, farms, forests, and other habitats.
description:
Join us for the first-ever Karnataka Rajyotsava Bird Count—Friday 30 October to Monday 2 November 2026. Let's celebrate Karnataka Rajyotsava by watching birds, together, across every corner of the state.

Every year on 1 November, Karnataka celebrates its formation—Karnataka Rajyotsava—a day that unites people across the state in pride for our language, land, and shared heritage. This year, the Karnataka birding community invites you to add a new tradition to the celebration: a statewide bird count.

From the coastal wetlands of Dakshina Kannada to the scrub forests of the Deccan plateau, the Western Ghats, and our lakes, gardens, and cityscapes, Karnataka is home to an extraordinary diversity of birds. Karnataka Rajyotsava Bird Count (KRBC) is our way of celebrating that richness—while together generating valuable, lasting data on the birds of Karnataka.

But be responsible! While you enjoy birdwatching during the count, ensure that you minimize disturbance to the birds and think carefully about the impact of your activities on birds and people at all times. Getting too close to a nest or disturbing a nest, or driving around on lake beds and grasslands, should be avoided.

Also be safe. Get good sleep, eat well, and ensure that you do not go close to elephants or any other dangers. If you perceive some areas to be unsafe, please avoid such areas or reach out to other people to form a group before going there.

details.when: 30 October to 2 November 2026. Participants could observe birds at any time during the four-day count.
details.where: Across Karnataka, including gardens, lakes, farms, forests, campuses, and other accessible habitats.
details.how:
• Watch birds for at least 15 minutes or more
  • Use eBird Mobile app to create and upload your bird lists
  • Each list should be a complete list along with counts of each species
details.challenges:
KRBC has three special challenges. Among the people who complete each challenge, one person (randomly drawn) will get a small token of appreciation from the Karnataka Bird Monitoring Network (KBMN).

Challenge 1: The challenge here is to cover as many of Karnataka’s 30 districts as possible. Participants who cover the maximum number of districts will be highlighted after the challenge. Here, at least four complete checklists, each of at least 15 minutes duration are required from each district for it to qualify.

Challenge 2: Some districts in Karnataka have more bird checklists than others. The challenge here is to cover as many districts with fewer than 10,000 complete checklists at the start of the count. Participants who cover the maximum number of these districts will be highlighted after the challenge. Here, at least four complete checklists, each of at least 15 minutes duration are required from each district for it to qualify. These are the qualifying districts.

Yadgiri, Haveri, Gadag, Kalaburagi, Koppal, Davanagere, Chitradurga, Bidar, Kolar, Belagavi, Raichur, Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Dharwad, Tumakuru, Hassan, Chikkaballapura

Challenge 3: Karnataka still has many parts that do not have any bird checklists. The challenge here is to cover as many 5km grid cells that do not have bird data at the start of the count. A KML file of these cells is linked here. Participants who cover the maximum number of previously unbirded cells will be highlighted after the challenge. Here, a single complete checklist of at least 15 minutes duration is sufficient from each cell.
details.additionalInformation:
• Complete Lists: List all the birds you were able to identify, by sight or sound, along with their counts, to the best of your ability.
  • Please upload all your lists before 10 November 2026.
  • You can watch birds on any or all days between 30 October and 2 November 2026.
  • You can watch from anywhere—your home, garden, terrace, park, farm, lake, forest, wetland… anywhere!
  • The count runs from midnight on 30 October to midnight on 2 November 2026.
  • You can make multiple checklists through the day—and also at dawn, dusk, or night!
  • Birders uploading their checklists outside Karnataka can share their checklists with eBird UserID: karnatakabirdcount.
details.tutorials: 'How to' videos are available to download and share.

pressRelease.title: Karnataka’s first statewide Rajyotsava Bird Count brings communities together
pressRelease.description: The four-day citizen-science event connected participants across all 31 districts to document local birdlife. The shared effort recorded 407 species and demonstrated how everyday observations can contribute to a statewide picture of biodiversity.

testimonials.quote: I enjoyed exploring new places, spotting different birds, and being part of a group effort to document Karnataka’s bird diversity. It was a wonderful experience to connect with bird lovers.
